# Universe24

> One line of whole-number arithmetic on a cubic lattice of Node-clocks, Rule3's carry its one division, read through clicks: the formulas it shares with nature and adds. A paper archived on Zenodo and at the tag v1.1.0, its supplement with every proof, the law of the lattice, the derivations as scripts, the engine, Tensor24 (src/tensor24/), with its tests and the paper's engine at the tag v1.1.0, and one world, Universe24: three files of whole numbers (examples/tensor24/), every Node-clock stepping by one act, the record read through the clicks by one decoder. The old engine left the working tree on 2026-10-30 and stands in git's history. Author: Alon Gonen, independent researcher, Haifa, Israel (ORCID 0009-0008-2701-4599). Licence MIT. Permanent record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436 (the concept DOI of the releases from 3.0.0 on, resolving to the latest version; the versions 1.1.0 to 2.1.0 under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113); the current software version, 4.0.0, Universe24: one Node, one universe, under the concept DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436 (the tag v4.0.0 is the owner's push of 2026-10-25, with no Zenodo version record; the concept DOI resolves to the latest Zenodo deposit (3.0.0)); 3.0.0: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466437

## In plain words

Suppose nature is discrete: space is made of Node-clocks, and between one Node-clock and the next nothing moves faster than light. A cubic centimetre then holds an astronomical number of Node-clocks, so no centre can know and decide for all of them; each Node-clock acts on its own, seeing only itself and its six neighbours. Tensor24 is that machine: a board of Node-clocks, each a set of gears that mesh with its six neighbours' gears through six Meshes, and one act at every Node-clock, alike everywhere, which the runner repeats in rounds. Every gear takes a push in whole numbers, turns by what its teeth carry and keeps the rest as its fine tooth, so nothing is lost and the run back returns the start bit for bit. Rule3's carry is the one division, with the remainder kept; there is no float, no root and no table, and every number stands in three files of whole numbers, a universe, a piece and a setting, none of which declares a particle, a mass or a coupling. Nothing of nature is typed: the physics is read from the clicks alone, a click being the carry's quotient where a winding is whole, whole or split, the one measurement. Time belongs to each Node-clock's own count; a round is an index from outside that no Node-clock reads. The act is built and tested while no clock moves; what happens when a clock moves, the strengths of the couplings, the notch, the shift and the shears and the clicks themselves are drafts and open items in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, section 6. The paper's one claim: the rule helps compute things in nature. The scripts that reproduce every number in the paper left the working tree on 2026-10-30 and stand in git (the tags v1.1.0 and v4.0.0).

## Read first

- [The paper, 40 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Paper.pdf): "Universe24: one simple rule, the formulas it shares with nature and adds" (Alon Gonen, 2026)
- [The supplement, Online Resource 1, 85 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/one_rule/Universe24_Supplement.pdf): the claims list and the algebraic steps of every derivation
- [The time paper, 22 pages](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/papers/spacetime_events/Universe24_Discrete_Spacetime_of_Events_Paper.pdf): "A discrete spacetime of events in whole numbers: why clocks slow, why nothing outruns light, and why time has a direction only where something was measured" (Alon Gonen, 2026), its source and run in papers/spacetime_events/ (its figure script and checks left the working tree and stand in git at the tag v4.0.0)
- [README](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/README.md): the aim, what stands (Tensor24, the old engine out), the law in four lines, the description of the system, how to run it, the documents, the papers
- [The architecture](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the one document that tells the system and the one the work runs from: the parts, the Node-clock first (the three files, the loader, the Node-clock, the runner, the record, the decoder, the visualizer, the guards), each told by the clock, the board and the clicks, with its algebra, home, test and status, and who may import whom

## The documents

- [The law of the lattice](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/docs/ALGEBRA.md): the project's seven postulates at its head in one place (the many Node-clocks with no centre and the locality they force; whole numbers for the reversibility of time; the speed of light at most; nature cyclic and no information lost; the Node-clock with no if; rates multiplying along a gear train, so the time gear's law linear in the logarithm of the rate; the board progressing in complexity with time, as a general idea), then one algebraic line per rule, a changed line holding its new wording alone and the former clauses standing by name in its closing section, the one Node-clock, the click's read of the great clock, the great clock reading itself, the trains at the click, the volume holder, and the turnover (cancelled, decision 27)
- [Contributing](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CONTRIBUTING.md): forks and pull requests, the ground rules, the checks, how to report an error or a failed reproduction
- [What changed](https://closer24.github.io/Universe24/CHANGELOG.md): what changed since the new engine, Tensor24; the earlier history stands in git

## The code

- [Repository on GitHub](https://github.com/Closer24/Universe24): the derivations as scripts (tools/derivations/), the implementation (src/tensor24/), the tests that prove the Node-clock's law (tests/), the one world's three files (examples/tensor24/), and the tools that check, run and decode it (tools/tensor24_files.py, tensor24_run.py, tensor24_decode.py)
- [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466436): the concept DOI of the releases from 3.0.0 on, the permanent record and the one to cite, resolving to the latest version (the versions 1.1.0 to 2.1.0 under [10.5281/zenodo.23190113](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190113)); the current software version, 4.0.0, Universe24: one Node-clock, one universe, stands under the concept DOI with no version record (the tag v4.0.0 is the owner's push of 2026-10-25, with no Zenodo version record; the concept DOI resolves to the latest Zenodo deposit (3.0.0)); 3.0.0, the click as one act, the spin and the atom, is [10.5281/zenodo.23466437](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23466437); the paper's engine, version 1.1.0, is 10.5281/zenodo.23202100
